newsHook: Building ground support equipment in County Tyrone that now works at airports in more than a hundred countries, and taking two innovation accolades this year with SkyBelt, is exactly the kind of story our readers do not hear often enough.
questions: Dungannon is a long way from the world's big airports. How did the company end up supplying more than a hundred countries from there?
SkyBelt took top honours this year. What problem on the ramp does it actually solve?
Ground support equipment is bought on whole-life cost and lives outdoors for twenty years. How does that shape what you build?
Airlines and handlers are under real cost pressure. Where does that show up in what they will and will not buy?
Electrification is coming to the ramp as well as the aircraft. How far along is that in practice?
You manufacture in Northern Ireland and export almost everything. What is the hardest part of that right now?
Where does Mallaghan go from here?

newsHook: Inventing a step-free boarding ramp in Telford so that wheelchair users and passengers with reduced mobility can board an aircraft with dignity, and selling it worldwide, is a story our readers would genuinely learn from.
questions: You built a step-free ramp because the existing options were not good enough. What were passengers actually being put through?
Accessible boarding is a legal duty and an operational headache. Which argument actually persuades an airport?
The ramp has to work in a turnaround measured in minutes. How do you make dignity fast?
You started in 2009 from Telford. What was the hardest year?
Airports buy slowly and in capital cycles. How do you sell into that as an independent business?
What do airlines and handlers still misunderstand about reduced mobility passengers?
Where does Aviramp go from here?
